analysis:
All eight units are documentation only. The PR adds a TTFT shape-warmup measurement report (docs/reports/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md), an index entry in docs/reports/README.md (line 7 on head), and a documented env var `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` in docs/reference/configuration.md (the patch hunk at about line 413). The reviewed text for configuration.md is the later excerpt (lines 520-687), which does not itself contain the new row. The row is visible only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated.

No runtime code is changed in the supplied evidence, so no control (attestation, E2E encryption, App Attest authorization, cache crypto) is altered by this diff. Consumer prompts (A-001) are not touched.

Security-relevant observations, none rising to a finding:
- The new env var is documented as forwarded to the LaunchAgent. It can only disable warmup (`0`, `false`, `no`, `off`) or skip the probe (`always`). The effect is a performance and availability trade-off, not a trust decision. It runs a 128-token probe plus shape cells with a 20 s per-engine budget. Listener-ready time rises from about 10 s to about 14.7 s on a cold cache (documented in the report), which is a minor startup-availability effect and is documented.
- The report uses throwaway .app bundles with fresh bundle IDs to simulate a cold shader cache. This is a benchmark method and does not affect the attestation or signing contract. The report states a binary MD5 for the build used. MD5 is a measurement identifier here, not a security control.
- The report states prefix cache was off during the runs and does not claim any production qualification.

Remaining question for integration: the actual implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupMode) is not in the supplied units. Whether warmup processes only synthetic tokens, and so avoids consumer data, cannot be verified here. This is an unverified contract, not a regression.
